plans.objective: [DIM: topological] The solution space exhibits a phase transition at $w \approx 2d$ (where $d$ is input dimension), beyond which the number of zero-violating solutions drops sharply; this reflects a change in the topology of the solution manifold from connected to fragmented. | pro: This hypothesis aligns with known results in algebraic geometry and neural network theory (e.g., the "double descent" phenomenon and manifold collapse in high-dimensional interpolation). It is testable via topological persistence or homology analysis of the solution set. con: Requires sophisticated tools (e.g., persistent homology) beyond standard ML pipelines; may be overkill for a simple width-scan experiment.

steps.description: Implement `family(kind, w, seed)` in `family.py` to define the constraint datasets. For Rigid family, generate linear constraints $y=x$ with $w$ points; for Fat family, generate sinusoidal constraints $y=a\sin(bx)+c$ with random parameters. Ensure inputs/outputs are reshaped to $(N, 1)$. Use `rng.standard_normal` for randomization. Ensure the Rigid family at width 64 achieves zero-violation (train_err $\le 1e-4$, val_err $\le 1e-3$) to serve as the anchor. The `capacity_scan` function will handle the width sweep (4–64), L-BFGS-B optimization, and multi-start (3 seeds) evaluation without modification to the core training loop.
